intro: Jesus went out of the house, sat by the sea side, and because great multitudes gathered, he entered a ship and taught the people on the shore in parables (Matthew 13:1-3). He later explained the parable of the sower to his disciples (Matthew 13:18).

questions.prompt: In the parable, what happened to the seeds that fell by the way side?
options: The fowls came and devoured them up
The sun scorched them
The thorns choked them
They brought forth thirtyfold
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:4 says some seeds fell by the way side, "and the fowls came and devoured them up."
questions.hint: Think of creatures that would find seed lying on a hard path.

questions.prompt: Why did the seeds on stony places wither away?
options: Because the fowls ate them
Because they had no root
Because the thorns sprung up
Because the sower stopped watering them
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:5-6 says these seeds sprang up quickly but were scorched when the sun was up, "and because they had no root, they withered away."
questions.hint: The text notes they lacked deepness of earth; what could not grow down into it?

questions.prompt: In his explanation, what does Jesus say happens when someone hears the word of the kingdom and understands it not?
options: He receives it with joy for a while
The care of this world chokes it
The wicked one catches away what was sown in his heart
He bears fruit an hundredfold
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:19 says that when one hears and understands not, "then cometh the wicked one, and catcheth away that which was sown in his heart," which is the seed by the way side.
questions.hint: This matches the seed that never got into the soil at all.

questions.prompt: According to Jesus' explanation, what chokes the word in the one who received seed among the thorns?
options: Tribulation or persecution
The care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches
The wicked one
Lack of deepness of earth
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:22 says that for the one who received seed among the thorns, "the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, choke the word, and he becometh unfruitful."
questions.hint: Tribulation is linked to the stony places; the thorns stand for two other pressures Jesus names.

intro: This parable is the closing illustration of the Sermon on the Mount, which Jesus taught after he "went up into a mountain" and his disciples came to him while the multitudes gathered (Matthew 5:1-2). When he finished, "the people were astonished at his doctrine" (Matthew 7:28).

questions.prompt: In the parable, where did the wise man build his house?
options: Upon a rock
Upon the sand
Beside a river
On top of a high hill
questions.explanation: Jesus likens the obedient hearer to "a wise man, which built his house upon a rock" (Matthew 7:24).
questions.hint: Think of the firmest foundation a builder could choose.

questions.prompt: When the rain, floods, and winds beat upon the foolish man's house, what happened to it?
options: It stood firm because the storm passed it by
It fell, and great was the fall of it
It was damaged only slightly and then repaired
The foolish man moved it to a safer place
questions.explanation: The foolish man built "upon the sand," and when the storm beat upon his house "it fell: and great was the fall of it" (Matthew 7:26-27).
questions.hint: Compare its outcome with the house in verse 25, which "fell not."

questions.prompt: According to Jesus, whom is he likening to the wise man who built on the rock?
options: Whoever hears his sayings but does not do them
Whoever teaches the law as the scribes do
Whoever hears his sayings and does them
Whoever builds the largest house
questions.explanation: Jesus says, "whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man" (Matthew 7:24).
questions.hint: Both builders heard; the difference lies in what came next.

questions.prompt: When Jesus ended these sayings, how did the people respond, and what reason does the narrator give?
options: They were astonished, for he taught as one having authority, and not as the scribes
They left angrily, because he contradicted the scribes
They asked him to explain the parable privately
They were silent, because they did not understand his words
questions.explanation: The narrator records that "the people were astonished at his doctrine: For he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes" (Matthew 7:28-29).
questions.hint: Read the two verses immediately following the parable.

intro: A certain lawyer stood up and tempted Jesus, asking, 'Master, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?' (Luke 10:25). After agreeing that the law commands love for God and neighbour, the lawyer, 'willing to justify himself,' asked, 'And who is my neighbour?' Jesus answered with this parable (Luke 10:29-30).

questions.prompt: In the parable, along which road was the man travelling when he fell among thieves?
options: From Jerusalem to Jericho
From Nazareth to Capernaum
From Bethlehem to Jerusalem
From Samaria to Galilee
questions.explanation: Jesus says, 'A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among thieves,' who left him half dead (Luke 10:30).
questions.hint: He 'went down' from the holy city toward a city near the Jordan.

questions.prompt: When the Samaritan left the inn the next day, what did he give the host to care for the wounded man?
options: Thirty pieces of silver
Two pence
A talent of gold
Ten pounds
questions.explanation: On the morrow the Samaritan 'took out two pence, and gave them to the host,' promising to repay any further cost when he returned (Luke 10:35).
questions.hint: It was a small number of coins, with a promise to cover anything more.

questions.prompt: After the lawyer said the neighbour was 'He that shewed mercy on him,' what did Jesus tell him?
options: Sell all that thou hast, and give to the poor
Go thy way; thy faith hath made thee whole
Go, and do thou likewise
Go and shew thyself to the priest
questions.explanation: Jesus asked which of the three was neighbour to the wounded man, and when the lawyer answered 'He that shewed mercy on him,' Jesus said, 'Go, and do thou likewise' (Luke 10:36-37).
questions.hint: Jesus turned the lawyer's answer into a personal instruction to imitate the Samaritan.

questions.prompt: What question from the lawyer directly prompted Jesus to tell this parable?
options: Which is the great commandment in the law?
Is it lawful to give tribute unto Caesar?
Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me?
And who is my neighbour?
questions.explanation: The lawyer, 'willing to justify himself, said unto Jesus, And who is my neighbour?' and Jesus answered with the story of the Samaritan (Luke 10:29).
questions.hint: The lawyer wanted to define one word from the commandment he had just quoted.

intro: Sitting in a ship by the sea, Jesus taught great multitudes gathered on the shore, speaking 'many things unto them in parables' (Matthew 13:1-3). These two short parables were spoken to that multitude (Matthew 13:34).

questions.prompt: In the first parable, where did the man sow the grain of mustard seed?
options: Among thorns
In his field
In a vineyard
On stony ground
questions.explanation: Jesus says the grain of mustard seed was one 'which a man took, and sowed in his field' (Matthew 13:31).
questions.hint: The man planted it on land that belonged to him.

questions.prompt: In the second parable, how many measures of meal did the woman hide the leaven in?
options: Two
Seven
Three
Ten
questions.explanation: The woman 'hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened' (Matthew 13:33).
questions.hint: It is a small number, one more than a pair.

questions.prompt: Both parables begin with the same comparison. What does Jesus say is like a grain of mustard seed and like leaven?
options: The temple in Jerusalem
The law of Moses
The city of Nineveh
The kingdom of heaven
questions.explanation: Jesus opens each parable with 'The kingdom of heaven is like', first to a grain of mustard seed and then to leaven (Matthew 13:31, 33).
questions.hint: Listen to the opening words Jesus repeats in both parables.

questions.prompt: According to Matthew right after these parables, why did Jesus speak to the multitude in parables?
options: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet
Because the disciples asked him to
Because the Pharisees forbade him to teach openly
Because the multitude could not hear him from the ship
questions.explanation: Matthew says Jesus spoke in parables 'That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying, I will open my mouth in parables' (Matthew 13:35).
questions.hint: Matthew connects this teaching style to words written long before.

batch.title: The Mustard Seed and the Leaven

intro: When a man in the crowd asked Jesus to make his brother divide the inheritance with him, Jesus refused to act as judge and warned them to beware of covetousness, then told this parable (Luke 12:13-15).

questions.prompt: When the rich man's ground brought forth plentifully, what problem did he say he had?
options: He had no room where to bestow his fruits
He had no servants to gather the harvest
He had no buyers for his grain
He had no heir to receive his goods
questions.explanation: The rich man thought within himself, 'What shall I do, because I have no room where to bestow my fruits?' (Luke 12:17).
questions.hint: Think about storage space for an unusually large harvest.

questions.prompt: What did the rich man decide to do with his barns?
options: Give them to his brother
Sell them to a neighbor
Pull them down and build greater ones
Open them to feed the poor
questions.explanation: He said, 'I will pull down my barns, and build greater; and there will I bestow all my fruits and my goods' (Luke 12:18).
questions.hint: His solution was about making more space for himself.

questions.prompt: After God called the man a fool, what conclusion did Jesus draw about such a person?
options: So is he that buildeth barns in the wrong season
So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God
So is he that refuseth to share with his brother
So is he that trusteth in his servants
questions.explanation: God told him his soul would be required that night, and Jesus concluded, 'So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God' (Luke 12:20-21).
questions.hint: Jesus contrasts treasure kept for oneself with being rich in another direction.

questions.prompt: What request prompted Jesus to warn the crowd to beware of covetousness and then tell this parable?
options: A man asked Jesus to heal his sick brother
A man asked whether to pay tribute to Caesar
A man asked Jesus to tell his brother to divide the inheritance with him
A man asked how to store his harvest
questions.explanation: One of the company asked Jesus to make his brother 'divide the inheritance with me'; Jesus replied that a man's life 'consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth' (Luke 12:13-15).
questions.hint: The dispute was between two brothers over family property.

intro: Publicans and sinners drew near to hear Jesus, and the Pharisees and scribes murmured, "This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them"; in answer, Jesus spake this parable unto them (Luke 15:1-3).

questions.prompt: When a man with an hundred sheep loses one, where does Jesus say he leaves the ninety and nine while he goes after the lost one?
options: In the wilderness
In the sheepfold at home
With a hired servant in the city
In the temple courts
questions.explanation: Jesus asks what man would not "leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it" (Luke 15:4).
questions.hint: Think of the open country where the flock was grazing.

questions.prompt: What does the woman who loses one of her ten pieces of silver do to find it?
options: She lights a candle, sweeps the house, and seeks diligently
She asks her neighbours to search the street for her
She waits until morning and then looks in the market
She borrows another piece of silver from a friend
questions.explanation: Jesus describes the woman who would "light a candle, and sweep the house, and seek diligently till she find it" (Luke 15:8).
questions.hint: She searches her own house carefully, needing light to see.

questions.prompt: After the parable of the lost coin, what point does Jesus himself state?
options: There is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth
Whoever loses what is entrusted to him shall be cast out
Silver laid up on earth is better kept than spent
The righteous shall be rewarded for never going astray
questions.explanation: Jesus concludes, "Likewise, I say unto you, There is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth" (Luke 15:10).
questions.hint: The finding in the story led to rejoicing; Jesus applies that rejoicing to heaven.

questions.prompt: What complaint from the Pharisees and scribes led Jesus to speak these parables?
options: "This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them"
"This man healeth on the sabbath day"
"This man teacheth that the temple shall be destroyed"
"This man's disciples wash not their hands"
questions.explanation: When publicans and sinners drew near to hear him, the Pharisees and scribes murmured that he received sinners and ate with them, and Jesus answered with this parable (Luke 15:1-3).
questions.hint: Look at who was gathering around Jesus at the start of the chapter.

batch.title: The Lost Sheep and the Lost Coin

intro: Publicans and sinners drew near to hear Jesus, and the Pharisees and scribes murmured, saying, "This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them" (Luke 15:1-2). In answer, Jesus told a series of parables about the lost being found, ending with this story of a father and his two sons (Luke 15:3, 11).

questions.prompt: What did the younger son ask his father to give him?
options: The portion of goods that fell to him
A ring for his hand and shoes for his feet
The fatted calf for a feast with his friends
A field of his own to farm
questions.explanation: The younger son said, "Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me," and soon took his journey into a far country (Luke 15:12-13).
questions.hint: He asked for his share before leaving home.

questions.prompt: After a mighty famine arose, what work was the younger son sent into the fields to do?
options: To keep the citizen's sheep
To feed swine
To dress a vineyard
To gather the harvest of wheat
questions.explanation: A citizen of that country sent him into his fields to feed swine, and he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat (Luke 15:15-16).
questions.hint: He longed to eat what these animals ate.

questions.prompt: When the elder son refused to join the celebration, what reason did the father give for making merry?
options: The younger son had returned with great wealth
The elder son had not served faithfully
His brother was dead and is alive again, was lost and is found
The servants had asked for a feast
questions.explanation: The father said, "It was meet that we should make merry, and be glad: for this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found" (Luke 15:32).
questions.hint: The father's answer echoes what he said when the son first came home (Luke 15:24).

questions.prompt: According to the opening of Luke 15, what prompted Jesus to tell the parables of this chapter?
options: His disciples asked him to teach them to pray
A lawyer asked him, "Who is my neighbour?"
Herod sought to kill him
The Pharisees and scribes murmured that he received sinners and ate with them
questions.explanation: When publicans and sinners drew near to hear him, the Pharisees and scribes murmured, "This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them," and Jesus spake this parable unto them (Luke 15:1-3).
questions.hint: Look at who was drawing near to Jesus and who objected.

intro: Peter came to Jesus and asked, "Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him?" (Matthew 18:21). Jesus answered him, then told this parable of a king settling accounts with his servants (Matthew 18:22-23).

questions.prompt: When the king began to reckon with his servants, how much did the first servant brought to him owe?
options: Ten thousand talents
An hundred pence
Thirty pieces of silver
Seven talents
questions.explanation: The servant brought to the king "owed him ten thousand talents," and the lord, moved with compassion, "forgave him the debt" (Matthew 18:24, 27).
questions.hint: It was an enormous sum, far greater than any servant could repay.

questions.prompt: What did the forgiven servant do to the fellowservant who owed him an hundred pence and begged for patience?
options: He cast him into prison till he should pay the debt
He forgave him the debt as he himself had been forgiven
He gave him more time and lent him more money
He brought him before the king to be judged
questions.explanation: He took his fellowservant by the throat, and when begged for patience "he would not: but went and cast him into prison, till he should pay the debt" (Matthew 18:28-30).
questions.hint: Compare how he treated his fellowservant with how the king treated him; he showed no mercy.

questions.prompt: After the king delivered the wicked servant to the tormentors, what lesson did Jesus draw for his hearers?
options: The heavenly Father will do likewise if they from their hearts forgive not every one his brother
Debts must always be repaid in full before any forgiveness is given
Servants should never take their complaints to their lord
Forgiveness is only required when the offender can pay back what is owed
questions.explanation: Jesus concluded, "So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses" (Matthew 18:35).
questions.hint: Look at the final verse, which begins "So likewise."

questions.prompt: Peter had suggested forgiving a brother "till seven times." How did Jesus answer him before telling this parable?
options: Until seventy times seven
Until seven times, as Peter said
Until three times, and then no more
Only until the brother repays what he owes
questions.explanation: Jesus told Peter, "I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven" (Matthew 18:22), and the parable follows as an illustration ("Therefore," Matthew 18:23).
questions.hint: Jesus explicitly rejected Peter's number and gave a far larger one.

intro: Jesus told this parable to His disciples right after Peter asked, "Behold, we have forsaken all, and followed thee; what shall we have therefore?" and Jesus answered that "many that are first shall be last; and the last shall be first" (Matthew 19:27-30). The parable opens with "For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder" (Matthew 20:1), illustrating that saying.

questions.prompt: What wage did the householder agree to pay the labourers he hired early in the morning?
options: A penny a day
Two pence a day
A talent for the season
A share of the vintage
questions.explanation: The householder "agreed with the labourers for a penny a day" and sent them into his vineyard (Matthew 20:1-2).
questions.hint: It was a single small coin, agreed before any work began.

questions.prompt: When the householder asked the men standing idle at the eleventh hour why they stood there all day, what did they answer?
options: They had just arrived from another city
They were waiting for higher pay
No man had hired them
They had finished work in another vineyard
questions.explanation: They replied, "Because no man hath hired us," and he sent them into the vineyard too (Matthew 20:6-7).
questions.hint: Their idleness was not by their own choice.

questions.prompt: After the householder defends paying everyone the same, what saying concludes the parable?
options: He that humbleth himself shall be exalted
So the last shall be first, and the first last
To whom much is given, much shall be required
The labourer is worthy of his hire
questions.explanation: The parable ends, "So the last shall be first, and the first last: for many be called, but few chosen" (Matthew 20:16).
questions.hint: Think about the order in which the workers were paid.

questions.prompt: The parable follows a question Peter asked Jesus. What had Peter asked?
options: How often he should forgive his brother
Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven
Whether it was lawful to pay tribute to Caesar
What the disciples would have, since they had forsaken all and followed Jesus
questions.explanation: Peter asked, "Behold, we have forsaken all, and followed thee; what shall we have therefore?" and Jesus' answer ended with "many that are first shall be last; and the last shall be first" (Matthew 19:27-30).
questions.hint: Peter's question concerned reward, much like the complaint of the first labourers.

intro: Jesus told this parable to His disciples, who had come to Him privately on the mount of Olives asking, "what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world?" (Matthew 24:3). It continues His answer about being ready for His coming, since "of that day and hour knoweth no man" (Matthew 24:36).

questions.prompt: In the parable, what did the foolish virgins fail to bring that the wise virgins brought?
options: Oil for their lamps
Wedding garments
Gifts for the bridegroom
Money to pay the porter
questions.explanation: The foolish "took their lamps, and took no oil with them," but the wise "took oil in their vessels with their lamps" (Matthew 25:3-4).
questions.hint: Think about what a lamp needs in order to keep burning.

questions.prompt: What happened while the foolish virgins went away to buy what they lacked?
options: The bridegroom came, the ready ones went in with him to the marriage, and the door was shut
The wise virgins fell asleep and missed the bridegroom
The bridegroom delayed his coming until morning so they could return
The bridegroom sent servants to search for them
questions.explanation: "While they went to buy, the bridegroom came; and they that were ready went in with him to the marriage: and the door was shut" (Matthew 25:10).
questions.hint: Consider who was able to go in, and what happened to the entrance afterward.

questions.prompt: What conclusion does Jesus Himself draw at the end of the parable?
options: Watch, because you know neither the day nor the hour when the Son of man comes
Share everything you have, so that no one goes without
Sleep is sinful, so never rest while waiting
The kingdom belongs only to those who buy their own oil at the market
keywords: neither the day nor the hour
questions.explanation: Jesus closes with, "Watch therefore, for ye know neither the day nor the hour wherein the Son of man cometh" (Matthew 25:13). Note that in the story both wise and foolish slept (Matthew 25:5); the difference was being prepared.
questions.hint: Look at the final verse, which begins with a command.

questions.prompt: This parable is part of Jesus' answer to a question. Who asked it, and what did they ask?
options: The disciples, privately on the mount of Olives, asking about the sign of His coming and the end of the world
The Pharisees in the temple, asking whether it was lawful to give tribute to Caesar
A lawyer, asking who his neighbour was
The multitude by the sea, asking for a sign from heaven
questions.explanation: "As he sat upon the mount of Olives, the disciples came unto him privately, saying, Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world?" (Matthew 24:3).
questions.hint: Look at the start of the previous chapter, where a small group approached Jesus away from the crowds.

intro: Luke records that Jesus spoke this parable "unto certain which trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and despised others" (Luke 18:9). It contrasts the prayers of two men who went up to the temple to pray (Luke 18:10).

questions.prompt: In his prayer, how often did the Pharisee say that he fasted?
options: Twice in the week
Once a month
Every day
Three times a year
questions.explanation: The Pharisee prayed, "I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess" (Luke 18:12).
questions.hint: He mentioned his fasting alongside giving tithes of all he possessed.

questions.prompt: How did the publican behave as he prayed?
options: He stood near the altar and lifted his hands toward heaven
He stood afar off, would not lift up his eyes, and smote upon his breast
He offered a lamb and thanked God that he was not like other men
He stood boldly and listed the good deeds he had done
questions.explanation: The publican, "standing afar off, would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven, but smote upon his breast, saying, God be merciful to me a sinner" (Luke 18:13).
questions.hint: Notice where he stood and what he did not dare to lift up.

questions.prompt: According to Jesus, which man went down to his house justified, and what principle did He give?
options: The Pharisee, because he gave tithes of all that he possessed
Both men equally, because both went up to the temple to pray
The publican, for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased, and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted
Neither man, because neither offered a sacrifice in the temple
questions.explanation: Jesus said the publican "went down to his house justified rather than the other: for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted" (Luke 18:14).
questions.hint: Think about which man exalted himself and which humbled himself.

questions.prompt: According to Luke, to whom did Jesus direct this parable?
options: To certain which trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and despised others
To His disciples, after they asked Him to teach them to pray
To a lawyer who asked, "Who is my neighbour?"
To publicans and sinners who drew near to hear Him
questions.explanation: Luke states that Jesus "spake this parable unto certain which trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and despised others" (Luke 18:9).
questions.hint: The audience shared an attitude much like the Pharisee's in the story.

intro: Sitting on the Mount of Olives, Jesus was answering His disciples' private question about the sign of His coming and of the end of the world (Matthew 24:3). He told this parable right after warning, "Watch therefore, for ye know neither the day nor the hour wherein the Son of man cometh" (Matthew 25:13).

questions.prompt: On what basis did the man travelling into a far country decide how many talents to give each servant?
options: To every man according to his several ability
According to how long each had served him
Equally, so that no servant would complain
According to which servant asked first
questions.explanation: The man gave five, two, and one talents "to every man according to his several ability" before he took his journey (Matthew 25:15).
questions.hint: Notice the phrase at the end of the sentence that lists the amounts of five, two, and one.

questions.prompt: When the lord returned, what reason did the servant who had received one talent give for hiding it in the earth?
options: He had been robbed and wanted to protect what was left
He was afraid, saying he knew his lord was an hard man
He had forgotten about the talent until the lord returned
He had lent it to a friend who had not repaid it
questions.explanation: The servant said, "I knew thee that thou art an hard man... And I was afraid, and went and hid thy talent in the earth" (Matthew 25:24-25).
questions.hint: His answer describes both his view of his lord and his own feeling.

questions.prompt: After ordering the one talent to be given to the servant with ten talents, what principle does the lord state?
options: The last shall be first, and the first last
Many are called, but few are chosen
Unto every one that hath shall be given, and from him that hath not shall be taken away even that which he hath
Whosoever exalteth himself shall be abased
keywords: unto every one that hath shall be given
questions.explanation: The lord explains the transfer with the words, "For unto every one that hath shall be given, and he shall have abundance: but from him that hath not shall be taken away even that which he hath" (Matthew 25:28-29).
questions.hint: The principle explains why the talent goes to the servant who already has the most.

questions.prompt: The parable begins with "For the kingdom of heaven is as a man travelling into a far country." What command immediately before it does this "For" connect to?
options: "Love your enemies, bless them that curse you"
"Go ye therefore, and teach all nations"
"Judge not, that ye be not judged"
"Watch therefore, for ye know neither the day nor the hour wherein the Son of man cometh"
questions.explanation: Jesus' command to watch, because no one knows the day or hour of the Son of man's coming, leads directly into this parable of a lord who returns "after a long time" (Matthew 25:13-14, 19).
questions.hint: Look at the last verse of the parable of the ten virgins, just before this one begins.
